A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the quark-gluons of the nucleon and pions, as well as their vector meson excitations, are the fundamental degrees of freedom of the nucleon, and the vector meson excitational spectrum is an important aspect of nucleon structure.

the quark-gluons are a major part of the nucleon, with a large tensor component in the ρ -meson coupling, and that the vector meson idea of dominance is a good description of the electromagnetic interaction of nucleons, and of pions, at distances ≲1 fm.

the quark-gluonic structure of the nucleons is not a simple, pointlike structure but a complicated structure with the size of the order of 1 2 fermi, and the quark-guon structure is not the only structure, the vector mesons also have an essential role.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vector meson model is not an accurate model for the nucleon electromagnetic form-factors at large momentum transfers.
there is a strong connection between the tensor coupling of the nucleon to the ρ-mesons and the quark-gluonic structure of the nucleons.
the quark-gluonic structure of nucleon is important at distances of the order of the inverse nucleon mass, which is the distance scale of the nucleon form factors.
